section.providers.title: Model providers
section.providers.description: Connect official APIs or third-party relays. Keys are encrypted on this computer and never uploaded.
section.skills.title: Skills
section.skills.description: Skills teach the agent how to do specific things. Enabled skills appear in the index every turn; “Always load” also puts the body in the system prompt.
section.mcp.title: MCP servers
section.mcp.description: Connect MCP servers running as local processes or remote addresses. Their tools go through the same permission checks and approvals as built-in tools.
mcp.empty: No MCP servers yet. Add a local process or remote address and its tools will appear in conversations.
mcp.new.title: Add MCP server
mcp.edit.title: Edit MCP server
mcp.form.description: Connects immediately after saving. Environment values and tokens are stored only in the local credential service.
mcp.enabled.hint: When disabled, it stops connecting and its tools are no longer offered to the model from the next turn.
mcp.delete.title: Delete “{{name}}”?
mcp.delete.description: This removes the configuration, saved token and environment values. Running conversations will no longer see its tools from the next turn.
mcp.field.name: Name
mcp.field.token.hint: Encrypted and stored in the local system keychain when saved.
mcp.field.token.keep: Already set; leave blank to keep it
mcp.field.env.name: Name
mcp.field.env.hint: Values are stored only in the credential service; leaving them blank keeps the current value.

section.permissions.title: Permissions & approvals
section.permissions.description: Decide what the agent may do right away and what it must ask you about first.
permissions.mode.label: Permission mode
permissions.mode.read-only.name: Read-only
permissions.mode.read-only.hint: Can only read files and search
permissions.mode.ask.name: Ask
permissions.mode.ask.hint: Asks before writing files or running commands
permissions.mode.auto.name: Auto
permissions.mode.auto.hint: Follows the rules; still asks for risky actions
permissions.rules.title: Rules
permissions.rules.order: When several rules match, deny wins over ask and ask wins over allow, regardless of order or scope.
permissions.rules.empty: No rules yet. Choose “Always allow” on an approval card, or add one here.
permissions.form.title: Add rule
permissions.form.pathHint: A glob relative to the project folder, such as src/** or **/.env*. Leave empty to match every call of this tool.
permissions.form.commandHint: * matches anything, such as npm test or git status*. Leave empty to match every command.
permissions.form.empty: With “Any tool”, enter a path, or the rule would match every action.
permissions.guard.ask: Whatever the rules say, these always ask again: recursive deletes, git push and force pushes, git reset --hard, privilege elevation, reading or writing sensitive files such as .env and private keys, and writing to .git. An allow rule that names the command can stop the prompt for risky commands like git push; Auto mode does not count.
permissions.guard.deny: Commands that would destroy data outside the workspace or the system (such as deleting the root or home folder, or formatting a disk) are denied outright.
